It also asserts that a field generating φ in that weak sense has the orbits as integral curves, which needs manifold calculus that A does not provide.

title: Iterated adjunction spaces in place of CW-complexes

title: Theorem 3.2 on a Euclidean space

title: A cell meeting a closed set in its boundary is attached to it
why: The two sides formalise disjoint halves of Milnor's remark. B is the coordinate fact: in a Morse chart, for small ε, e^λ ∩ M^{c-ε} = ė^λ (on e^λ, η = 0, so f = c - ξ), and e^λ is a closed λ-cell with boundary ė^λ. B is proved outright (B_holds, without A): choose ε with the √ε-disk inside the chart's target; the homeomorphism is q ↦ ε^{-1/2}·(first λ coordinates of y q), with inverse z ↦ y⁻¹(pad(√ε z)). A is the part Milnor 'does not argue' and B deliberately omits: a closed set plus a cell meeting it exactly in its boundary sphere is the adjunction space (pushout in TopCat), with the homotopy-equivalence corollary. So A ⇒ B holds only because B is true. B ⇒ A fails genuinely: B says nothing about pushouts.

title: Theorem 3.2 in a Morse patch, and on a submanifold

The latter does the in-patch argument on any T2 space but takes Assertion 3 (SDR of M^{c+ε} onto F⁻¹(-∞,c-ε]) as a hypothesis. A ⇒ B fails: Assertion 3 on an abstract manifold is Theorem 3.1 for F there, which the project does not have; patch_theorem_3_2 assumes it. B ⇒ A fails: patch_theorem_3_2 (arbitrary T2 space, hypothetical SDR) and the extension lemma are not consequences of B.

It concludes a strong deformation retraction of N^{c+ε} onto the explicit subspace N^{c-ε} ∪ ⋃ e_p, with explicit pairwise disjoint embedded cells. B is for abstract (Hausdorff, not necessarily second-countable) manifolds and concludes only a homotopy equivalence with some iterated adjunction space. So A ⇒ B fails for lack of an embedding theorem plus the (missing) Lemma D / cell-complex glue. B ⇒ A fails because A's conclusion is much stronger (SDR onto explicit embedded cells). A's second conjunct (isFiniteCellComplexType_union_cells) is a general-topology lemma about arbitrary Hausdorff spaces that B says nothing about. These are genuine differences, not just proof effort.

title: The Poincaré–Hopf integer

B: for holomorphic w : ℂᵏ → ℂⁿ with injective dw(0) and v real-orthogonal to range dw(0), (1) ⟨v, dw(0)z⟩ = 0 and (2) ⟨v, w(z)⟩ = const + Σ b_hj z^h z^j + o(‖z‖²). A ⇒ B: (1) is A with T = range dw(0); (2) is a second-order Taylor expansion proved outright from Mathlib's power series (isBigO_sub_partialSum_pow, coefficients p₂(e_h, e_j)), its linear term killed by (1). B ⇒ A: B for w = id on ℂ¹ and v' = conj⟨a,v⟩·e₀ gives ⟨a, v⟩ = 0, the hypothesis holding because conj(z)·a ∈ T. Clause (2) of B (the Taylor expansion Milnor writes) is content A does not state, but it is pure Mathlib analysis; the mathematical content Milnor's parenthesis asserts (linear terms vanish) is exactly A.

title: The Hessian of $L_p$ in holomorphic coordinates
why: A (universes 0): for w : V → F complex-C² at q (V, F arbitrary complex normed/inner product spaces) and any p, the real Hessian of z ↦ ‖w z − p‖² at q is 2(Re⟨dw v, dw v'⟩ + Re⟨w q − p, d²w(v, v')⟩) — the project's replacement for Milnor's 'clearly Q' determines the second fundamental form'. B: for an analytic immersion w : ℂᵏ → ℂⁿ at 0 and a unit vector v real-orthogonal to the ∂X/∂ξᵢ (X = realified w), there is a complex b with Re⟨v, w(x+iy)⟩ = const + Re Σ b_hj z^h z^j + o(‖ξ‖²) and B's (v·ℓ_ij) (normal projection of ∂²X/∂ξᵢ∂ξⱼ, paired with v) equals the polar form of Q' = Re Q. A ⇒ B not proved: B needs (i) a second-order Taylor expansion of the holomorphic ⟨v, w⟩ with a COMPLEX quadratic term (power series, as in V5_5), its linear term killed by the real-orthogonality hypothesis, and (ii) the identification of B's realified second derivatives/normal projection with the Hessian of f(ξ) = Re⟨v, w(toCk ξ)⟩ and of that Hessian with the polar form of Q' (power-series uniqueness: 2·p₂ = d²f). B is believed true (sketch checked: v ⊥ tangent makes ⟨v, P^⊥ ∂²X⟩ = ∂²f, and d²f is J-anti-invariant since f = Re of a holomorphic function). B ⇒ A holds only vacuously: A re-proved by the project's own computation; B (analytic immersions, normal unit v, finite dimension) cannot give A's formula for arbitrary C² maps and arbitrary p.

title: Global solutions of linear equations

why: A (universes 0; IsGeodesicFrom/expDom/exp definitions: exp_q v = γ(1) for a chosen geodesic γ on an open (-δ,1+δ) with γ0=q, γ'0=v, junk q): exp_q v = γ(1) for every such γ, exp_q 0 = q (q ∈ N), exp_q(tv) = γ(t) on (-δ,1+δ), a geodesic on (0,1) that is a smooth curve in N is the ray t ↦ exp_{γ0}(tγ'0) on [0,1], and a membership criterion for expDom. B: abstract manifold, LC connection, exp via geodesics on the CLOSED [0,1] (velocity within [0,1], HEq): (i) exp_q v = γ(1) and exp_q(tv) = γ(t) on [0,1], (ii) uniqueness of such γ on [0,1], (iii) exp_q defined for ‖v‖ small. A ⇒ B fails genuinely: B is about an abstract Hausdorff ℝⁿ-manifold with a smooth Mathlib RiemannianBundle and an ARBITRARY Mathlib CovariantDerivative that is Levi-Civita in Milnor's sense (IsLC: smooth, symmetric via mlieBracket, compatible = parallel fields, defined through ∃ D obeying axioms (a)–(c), keep inner products); the project has only slice submanifolds N ⊆ V with the induced metric/connection and no abstract geodesic theory (no Christoffel symbols, no D/dt or geodesic ODE in charts), and Whitney does not help since B's metric/connection need not be induced (no Nash embedding). B ⇒ A fails: B does not specialize to N ⊆ V without a bridge (↥N with ChartedSpace ℝⁿ, induced metric as RiemannianBundle, induced connection as CovariantDerivative proved IsLC, and a dictionary IsGeodesic/expMap/arcLen ↔ IsGeodesicOn/exp/pathLength), which the project does not have. Content also differs: B's (iii) (existence for small v) is not among A's listed theorems (it is V7_8's exists_exp_eq), and A's initial-ray and expDom statements are not in B.

label: restated
title: Normal radius
issue: `nrm q w := ‖(w : TangentSpace q)‖` is elaborated WITHOUT the RiemannianBundle instance (not in scope for that definition), so it is the Euclidean (PiLp) norm of the model vector w ∈ ℝⁿ, i.e. of the coordinates of w in chartAt q, not the Riemannian norm. Hence tball / IsNormBall (and IsUniformNormal (3)) use chart-dependent coordinate balls instead of Milnor's metric ε-balls (‖v‖, inner, arcLen elsewhere in B do use the Riemannian structure).
why: The item lists only definitions (NormalCoord hN q ε: exp_q on {v ∈ T_qN | ‖v‖ < ε} with a smooth inverse G on an open U; IsNormalRadius := Nonempty NormalCoord; expToN; expDiffeo, a PartialDiffeomorph ball 0 ε → N), so A = True and B ⇒ A is trivial (vacuous). B is a theorem (Lemma 10.3 (3): a uniform normal radius ε on a neighbourhood W of p) about abstract manifolds, which A = True cannot give; the definitions cannot be proved to agree because they live in different settings (embedded N ⊆ V vs abstract M). Vocabulary comparison: the project's normal radius uses the ambient norm on T_qN ⊆ V, which IS the induced Riemannian norm (faithful), whereas B's IsNormBall uses `nrm`, a chart-coordinate Euclidean norm (B_issue), so B's 'normal ball' is not Milnor's. With this bug, B depends on the arbitrary choice of chartAt q: it is plausibly FALSE for an atlas whose chart scale degenerates near p (e.g. a round circle with chartAt q = λ_q·(arc-length chart), λ_q → 0 as q → p: then the coordinate ε-ball at q has Riemannian radius ε/λ_q > π and exp_q is not injective on it) — not proved.
